newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX treads water in pre-bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX treads water in pre-bourse trade.

text.p: German shares treaded water in the run-up to bourse trade on Wednesday, as market uncertainty over the Bonn/Bundesbank row over revaluation continued to upset sentiment, despite soothing statements from both sides.
By 0746 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 4.37 points at 3,659.96 points, trading in a tight range after a strong advance earlier, with support at 3,650 points holding.
"The dollar is helping us this morning, and the debt market seems to be settling down a little bit too, which also helps," a Frankfurt trader said.
The dollar stood at 1.7318/20 marks pre-bourse.

Earlier in the day, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said that the German government and the Bundesbank had reached a common language and way of proceeding on a planned revaluation of central bank assets.
He also said that he and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer would do their best to have windfall funds created by the revaluation transferred to Bonn from 1998 and not earlier.

The decision had a fairly neutral effect on the market, despite the fact that uncertainty about the future of European currency union had translated into negative sentiment in the equity market of late.
Among the big winners pre-bourse was Continental AG, which rose 1.35 marks, or 3.46 pct, to 40.40 marks.
The German financial newsletter Platow Brief said Conti expected to report a distinct increase in 1997 profit at its annual meeting.
Germany's large utilities were also higher early on, enjoying a cyclical upturn, although they pared gains as electronic trade progressed.
Viag AG was up five marks, or 0.64 percent, at 785 marks, while Veba was up 23 pfennigs, or 0.23 percent at 97.45 marks.
Dollar strength also boosted car stocks, particularly Volkswagen, which rose 9.80 marks or 0.84 percent, to 176.80 marks.
Adidas and Puma rose 0.81 percent and 0.91 percent respectively, as the shares clawed back some ground lost after the sector fell in the wake of a profit warning by Nike.
Shares in Deutsche Telekom were also higher, after Wolfgang Schaeuble, Kohl's lieutenant, said that the sale of the government stake in the company would be done in a way that would not upset shares.
Telekom shares were up 48 pfennigs, or 1.26 percent, at 38.70 marks.
